paras: The attempted lynching of John Fish was an episode in Duke Centre, McKean County, Pennsylvania, reported in December 1880, in which a posse went to Fish's house intending to lynch him. Fish had already fled, and no one was harmed. The episode survives in a single paragraph of Pennsylvania state news, which does not give Fish's race.

According to the report, the authorities of Duke Centre were seeking Fish, whom the paper called "a notorious character." He was accused of having enticed "a number of girls" to the town "for immoral purposes," a charge the item stated as fact.

A posse then went to Fish's house "to lynch him," but found that he had fled. The report gives no date, time of day or size for the posse, and does not say who made it up or whether the authorities had any part in it.
No report of Fish's capture, an arrest of anyone in the posse, or a trial appears in the coverage.

The Juniata Sentinel and Republican of Mifflintown printed the story on December 22, 1880, as one of some two dozen "State Items," between an account of a girl's remains found in the woods and a powder accident in Cambria County. The two-sentence item reported the posse's aim without comment and treated the accusation against Fish as established. No other paper's version, local account or follow-up was found, and the item makes no reference to race.
